statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk 3% (low) with no Nasdaq-100 price path observable inside the CME weekend halt, against Stress of 66% (high) as Iran ties any Strait of Hormuz reopening to seven stated conditions while the G7 releases 100 million barrels of crude and diesel reserves.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold, so the mapped policy state stays EA_ON. A narrow danger window is published across the 22:00Z CME reopen and the hour after it, 00:00-02:00 Berlin on 5 October, where the published forecast Tail path reaches the WATCH band on gap and discontinuity risk rather than on observed structure.
headline: Iran names seven conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz and OPEC+ holds November output, turning the weekend's open checkpoints into stated positions while the CME halt keeps Tail at its floor and a 100-million-barrel G7 release caps the oil premium
body:
CME equity-index futures have been halted since Friday 21:00Z and reopen at 22:00Z on 4 October, so no Nasdaq-100 price path exists to assess and Tail stays at its structural floor of 3%. The last observed structure was orderly two-way behaviour. The cash index traded to an all-time intraday high of 31,017.53 on Friday 2 October, fully retraced it, and finished at a record 30,807.93, up 1.00% from a 30,501.56 previous close, in the lower half of its 30,737.07-31,017.53 range. VIX settled at 15.31, down 6.59%, after a 15.30-16.24 range. A record high that is fully retraced into the close is the opposite of the shallow-pullback, repeated-extension structure that Tail measures.

Stress is marked down two points to 66% from the 68% published an hour earlier, thirteen points below the 79% ceiling reached at 09:00Z. The reason is the character of the remaining risk rather than drift: the weekend's open checkpoints have become stated positions. OPEC+ confirmed in an official statement that its seven core members, Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan and Oman, will maintain September 2026 required production for November, a joint quota of 31 million barrels a day, with the next review on 1 November. Separately, Iran's parliament speaker stated that the Strait of Hormuz will not be opened until seven conditions based on the Islamabad memorandum are realised, among them a halt to U.S. strikes, an end to the naval blockade and the release of frozen assets. Iran's foreign minister added that the strait could reopen within a week if those terms were accepted, and backchannel contact through Qatari intermediaries is reported to remain active. A stated constraint with a named reopening path is a different risk object from an open question, and it argues for easing Stress rather than raising it.

The supply response is the second offset. The G7 agreed on 2 October to release up to 100 million barrels of crude and diesel through the International Energy Agency over four months, roughly 830,000 barrels a day, with a substantial diesel tranche in the first 20 days. Brent fell briefly below $100 before stabilising at $102.25, and WTI reached a one-month low of $88.06 before recovering to $91.11, down 1.90%.

Three weekend items argue against easing Stress further. The Houthis claim a ballistic-missile and drone strike on an Aramco site in Riyadh and fires were visible there on Saturday, but neither Saudi authorities nor Aramco has confirmed a cause, so no supply loss is established. UKMTO reported a further tanker struck by an unknown projectile about four nautical miles east of Oman, with engine-room damage and the crew safe; 31 of 48 projectile incidents since 6 July have occurred on that southern Omani route and Hormuz traffic is around 75% below pre-conflict levels. The U.S. has also moved the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group and the USS Makin Island amphibious group toward the region, adding roughly 9,000 personnel by late October. The strait has been effectively closed since 28 February 2026, so each of these is an incremental datapoint inside an existing regime rather than a new regime.

The rate path remains the clearest equity-side offset. September payrolls were soft enough to lift the unemployment rate to 4.2% from 4.1%, and odds of an October 0.25% hike have fallen from 64.2% a week earlier to roughly 17-23%, with only about 0.22% of further tightening priced through end-2026. The H.15 release of 2 October shows the 2-year at 4.78%, the 10-year at 5.24% and the 30-year at 5.61%, with the federal funds effective rate at 3.88%. None of yields, VIX, oil or breadth is currently aligned in a way that would amplify a one-way index path.

Confidence is raised to 88%. Current index, volatility, yield and oil levels are verified against primary sources, the OPEC+ outcome is an official statement, the Iranian position and the G7 release are verified in reputable current reporting, the tanker and Aramco items are verified with their confirmation status stated explicitly, and the seven-day U.S. calendar is complete. The one material gap is unchanged and structural: the weekend halt means there is no live price path, which is why Tail is published as a floor rather than as a measurement. The shared Finviz context file was last collected on 29 September and reports partial collection, so it is stale under the 90-minute freshness rule and was not used.

lookbackSummary: Across the past 24 published hours Claude held Tail at 3% in every slot, while Stress rose from 53% at 13:00Z on 3 October to a 79% ceiling at 09:00Z on 4 October and then eased to 73% at 10:00Z, 70% at 11:00Z and 68% at 12:00Z as the weekend's open checkpoints resolved. Confidence stayed in the 83-87% band. Every hour mapped to EA_ON and green, and the dominant mode was normal throughout.
outlookSummary: The closed Sunday session carries no scoreable Nasdaq-100 structure, so Tail is held between 3% and 6% through 20:00Z while Stress is marked down to 66% on the stated Iranian position and the G7 release. Tail then steps to 10% in the final closed hour and is raised to 21% and 20%, inside the WATCH band, across the 22:00Z CME reopen and the hour after it, which together form the published danger window. It decays conditionally to 8% by 11:00Z on 5 October on the assumption that price discovery is orderly, an assumption that a reopen gap extending without meaningful retracement would invalidate. Confidence troughs at 78% at the reopen and recovers to 87% once a continuous path is observable again.

Cross-assets not aligned in a way that would amplify a one-way path

forecast.analysis: Pre-reopen hour. Tail is raised to 10% because weekend news flow has to be absorbed into a single opening print rather than through continuous trading. The direction of that print is not predictable from available evidence, so the increment is discontinuity risk only.
drivers: Weekend flow to be absorbed into one opening print at 22:00Z
Gap direction not inferable from available evidence
Confidence trimmed into the unobservable transition

forecast.analysis: CME reopen hour. Tail is raised to 21%, inside the WATCH band, on gap and discontinuity risk rather than on any observed structure. Should an opening gap extend without a meaningful retracement, that would be the first genuine mean-reversion-failure evidence of the week; an orderly two-way open would invalidate it.
drivers: Reopen checkpoint: CME equity-index futures resume at 22:00Z
Mapped policy state moves to WATCH on discontinuity risk
Invalidation: an orderly two-way open with normal retracement
Confirmation: gap extension with shallow or absent pullbacks

forecast.analysis: Second danger-window hour. Tail is held at 20% and remains in the WATCH band while early liquidity is thin and a gap, if one prints, would not yet have been tested. Whether repeated extension follows is the conditional question this hour resolves; it is not an observation.
drivers: Thin early liquidity in the first hour after the reopen
Conditional checkpoint: is an opening gap tested or extended
Tail stays in the WATCH band pending first evidence

forecast.analysis: Tail decays to 14% on the assumption that the reopen produced orderly two-way price discovery, which is the modal outcome given a subdued 15.31 VIX settle and a fully retraced Friday high. Sustained one-way extension through this hour would invalidate the decay path.

Subdued VIX settle supports the orderly assumption

forecast.analysis: Conditional decay continues as a continuous price path becomes observable again and Confidence recovers with it. Stress eases to 65% because the weekend checkpoint stack is behind the market: OPEC+ decided, the G7 release announced, and Iran's position publicly stated.
drivers: Continuous price path observable again; Confidence recovering
Weekend checkpoint stack resolved rather than pending
Conditional on retracements having occurred after the reopen

forecast.analysis: Asian session underway. Tail at 10% assumes the reopen gap, if any, has been at least partially filled and that volatility is decaying. Regional equity reaction to the Hormuz headlines is the hour's conditional checkpoint rather than an established fact.

Assumes partial gap fill and decaying volatility
Checkpoint: regional reaction to the weekend Hormuz headlines

forecast.analysis: Tail at 9% on continued conditional normalisation. With no U.S. macro release inside this window, the hour's risk is headline-driven: a confirmed supply loss at the Riyadh facility, still unconfirmed at the assessment cutoff, is the main path that would reverse the decay.
drivers: No scheduled U.S. macro release inside this hour
Reversal path: confirmation of an actual Riyadh supply loss
Conditional normalisation assumed, not observed

forecast.analysis: Hold at 9% through the Asian afternoon. Stress eases to 62% as the G7 barrels begin to be framed against the closure: roughly 830,000 barrels a day of coordinated release is a partial offset to a strait that has been effectively closed since 28 February 2026.
